gaps.name: Full-sentence claims
gaps.need: Each claim stays a full sentence, and structure is optional. Agent Memory keeps hedged or conditional statements whole, and compares claims without structure through recorded judgments.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory splits each statement into entities, attributes, and relations. A full sentence stays only as raw turn text or a text chunk, and reconciliation never compares those. A sentence in an attribute value meets another claim only on the same entity, key, and scope.
gaps.ask_surrealdb: Ask for a statement field beside the triple. This does not bring back opaque chat history.

gaps.name: Trust from current evidence
gaps.need: One change to the trust of a source re-weights every claim that the source touched, in one action. Trust always follows the current source weights and decay settings. A read can show the trust of a claim at a past date.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory fixes the confidence of a value when it writes the value, and compares stored numbers at write time. Agent Memory lowers the trust of a source after repeated supersession, but the docs show no way to re-weight stored values. No API lets a caller change the trust of a source.
gaps.ask_surrealdb: Ask for trust that is calculated at read time beside the stored record, as an option for each Context. The stored values stay auditable.

gaps.name: Contradiction ladder
gaps.need: Agent Memory itself judges contradictions that are not exact matches, such as opposite, narrower, or equivalent claims. Each verdict records its method. A person gets each unclear or low-confidence verdict. Agent Memory checks stored pairs again when the claims on a topic change.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Reconciliation matches exact keys and makes no model call. Any value that differs is a conflict, and the docs define no looser match. So 4 kg against 4.0 kg is likely a conflict, and claims under different keys never meet. Extraction can flag a contradiction with stored memory as an uncertainty, but the docs do not say how. A judge for opposite or equal values on one key needs a new feature. Narrower claims, and claims under different keys, need a change to the data model.
gaps.ask_surrealdb: Ask for data about keys, such as single-valued, unit, and tolerance. This does not pin the list of keys.

gaps.name: Narrower scoped value
gaps.need: A narrower value, such as a Q4 figure, is returned only when its own statistics support it. Otherwise the read returns the broader value, and marks the narrower claim as not selected.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Values carry no unit, sample size, or standard error, and the docs show numbers sent as text. Only relations take a validity range, through valid_from and valid_until. An attribute such as a Q4 figure can hold its condition only in the access scope. No rule chooses between a narrower value and a broader value.

gaps.name: Author-only supersession
gaps.need: Only the holder of a claim, or a named successor, can replace the claim. A statement from another user that conflicts stays as a separate claim, and Agent Memory shows the two claims as a dispute.
gaps.agent_memory_today: A newer value replaces the old value when both have the same scope and the same source kind, such as two conversation turns. Keys in the context category are an exception, because they can keep several live values. The author does not count. A value from a different source kind never replaces the stored value, and Agent Memory creates an uncertainty record. A separate scope for each author protects authorship, but then Agent Memory raises no dispute between the scopes. A correction with no score replaces the old value. A scored correction below the confidence floor, default 0.7, or below the stored confidence does not.

gaps.name: Trust and evidence on hits
gaps.need: Each search hit carries its trust, its evidence, and its flags. The evidence is each source, each author, and the dates. The flags show open disputes and revised inputs. Agent Memory calculates the trust itself (see M2).
gaps.agent_memory_today: Each hit shows a score and its record kind, such as attribute or chunk. Where known, it also shows when Agent Memory learned the fact. The trust filter is “not supported yet”. Entity reads, but not search hits, return a stored confidence.

gaps.name: Belief stages
gaps.need: A claim moves from hypothesis to rule when its evidence holds for seven days. The check counts distinct statements, sources, and authors. Agent Memory runs the check itself, and never moves a promoted claim back automatically.
gaps.agent_memory_today: No fact has a stage, and no setting holds a threshold or a window. Consolidation writes a new record, not a higher stage. The promotion that SurrealDB plans moves a fact to a wider scope. In MemBrain, a wider scope is a change of layer, not of stage.

gaps.name: Assertion bands
gaps.need: Each returned claim carries a band: settled, attributed, tentative, contested, or historical. A settled claim needs a stage of rule or higher and independent sources. Agent Memory calculates the band at each read.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory has parts for four of the bands, but returns no band. Open uncertainties show disputes, and history shows replaced values. No field counts independent sources. Consolidation records carry a proof_count, but the docs do not say what it counts.

gaps.name: Layer precedence
gaps.need: For each user, the current claim of that user wins. Org knowledge outranks team knowledge, and team knowledge outranks individual knowledge. The other positions stay visible.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Scope says where a fact belongs, and grants say who can read it. Scope also decides if two values conflict at all, because values in different scopes coexist. No rule chooses which value wins.

gaps.name: Human approval
gaps.need: A person approves each change to team or org knowledge before the change is current. Agent Memory holds the proposals in a review queue, and its background passes also go through the queue. A decision applies only to the pair that the person judged.
gaps.agent_memory_today: No proposal state or review queue exists. Preview mode and a dry run show changes without a commit. Anyone with write access to a scope can settle a conflict. Background passes write into shared scopes with no approval step. When a person resolves one conflict, Agent Memory replaces every other value that conflicts on that entity and key, not only the judged pair.

gaps.name: Stale-input flags
gaps.need: A claim records the claims that it derives from. When one of those inputs changes, each read flags the claim, and the review queue receives it.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory keeps lineage only for facts that it derives itself. A caller cannot declare lineage on a write. A cached chat answer is not reused once a cited fact changes, but derived facts get no flag.

gaps.name: Succession
gaps.need: When a person leaves, a person names a successor. The successor can then revise, retract, and share the claims of the leaver, and the claims keep their original holder.
gaps.agent_memory_today: An admin can give the successor write access to the scope of the leaver, and the successor can act on behalf of the leaver. No record says who succeeds whom. The docs do not say how to retire a principal and keep its history.

gaps.name: Fact conditions
gaps.need: A fact can carry conditions, such as “Q4 only”, apart from its scope. The conditions are part of the conflict key, and a rule selects which value a read returns.
gaps.agent_memory_today: A caller can add an extra scope path, such as season/q4. Then readers need permission on that path, and no rule selects one value. Labels only filter results, and take no part in conflicts.

gaps.name: Name aliases
gaps.need: Different names for one entity resolve to one record. A person can merge two records, and can undo the merge later.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Names must match exactly, after Agent Memory removes differences of case, spaces, and Unicode form. The duplicate check returns no candidates. An alias table exists and reads follow it, but nothing in the product can write to it.

gaps.name: Valid-time query
gaps.need: A query can ask what was true on a date, what Agent Memory knew on a date, or both together. This works on every read, over REST and over MCP.
gaps.agent_memory_today: The time filter on search uses the date when Agent Memory learned a fact. Entity reads also accept validFrom and validUntil, but the docs do not define what they select. The docs contradict themselves about relations that ended. A soft forget also hides a fact from reads at an earlier time, so it changes past answers. The MCP tools page agrees for asOf reads. It adds that a system-time read (atInstant) from before the forget still sees the fact.

gaps.name: Share one fact
gaps.need: A holder can share one claim with a named colleague, and can revoke the share later. A record shows each grant and each revocation, so an auditor can find who had read access, and when.
gaps.agent_memory_today: To share one fact with one more reader, its writer must give it a second scope clause at write time. No endpoint changes the scope of a stored fact, and the share endpoint returns 501. An admin can add and revoke grants on scope paths, but a grant opens every fact at that path. Agent Memory logs scope changes, but /audit does not return them.

gaps.name: Redact erasure
gaps.need: Erasure removes personal content but keeps the records, the links, and the history. The legal sign-off of MB-77 now applies to the erasure of Agent Memory.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Soft forget hides facts but keeps the content. Purge deletes the facts, their history, and their links. Redaction of personal data works only at ingest.
gaps.ask_surrealdb: Ask for a redact mode beside purge. The legal sign-off for Spreetail is still open.

gaps.name: Expiry off switch
gaps.need: Spreetail can switch off expiry, so that a fact ends only by revision or retraction, never by age.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Only facts in the context category expire, after 7 days. Knowledge and identity facts never expire by age. A caller can set the category on each write, but no setting changes or switches off the 7-day expiry.

gaps.name: Async extraction
gaps.need: A conversation write returns before extraction runs. Thus a slow or failed model does not delay or block the capture of new facts.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Extraction on facts and turns completes before the API returns. Only document upload is asynchronous. A write with infer set to none skips extraction, but then Agent Memory extracts no facts from it.
gaps.ask_surrealdb: Ask for an opt-in mode. The default stays synchronous for other customers.

gaps.name: Durable background work
gaps.need: The background work of Agent Memory never loses or repeats work after a restart. It handles changes in commit order where order matters (MB-39). This durability applies to the background parts of extraction, promotion (F3), review queues (F6), and stale-input flags (F7). A caller can tell when a document job is complete.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Turn extraction is synchronous, so the API return marks its completion. Document extraction runs on a job queue, and a caller polls GET /documents/{id} to see when a job is complete. No notification tells the caller. The background consolidation pass keeps a watermark, and Agent Memory records audit events for background jobs. The docs do not say if extraction jobs, consolidation, or elaboration resume after a restart without loss or repeats.

gaps.name: Rules on every write path
gaps.need: The belief rules hold on every write path in Agent Memory. Examples are no silent overwrite, one-for-one replacement, revision only by the holder, and no instruction from a document. Agent Memory rejects a write that breaks a rule, and applies no part of it. Every read follows replacements to the current claim, and every interface returns the same numbers without content that the caller cannot read.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory offers no way to add custom rules. The docs call the model settings “five hooks”, but each one only picks a model for one stage. The docs say that every write runs through the reconciler. They name three invariants: “provenance is mandatory, supersession is non-destructive, and uncertainty is representable”. They give no fuller list of the rules that Agent Memory enforces. The docs do not say if trust uses evidence that the caller cannot read.

gaps.name: No instructions from documents
gaps.need: Content from a document never becomes an instruction or a preference. At most, it becomes a claim about what the document says. SurrealDB must confirm this behaviour in a written answer.
gaps.agent_memory_today: The docs do not answer this, and two pages disagree. Document extraction uses the same schema as turns, and that schema includes instructions. Yet the document stage lists only entities, attributes, relations and actions. The injection scanner rejects a write with a score of 0.7 or more. So if documents do yield instructions, a sentence below 0.7 can become one.

gaps.name: Entra sign-in per user
gaps.need: Users sign in with Microsoft Entra, and each user gets a credential of their own. Thus no Spreetail proxy holds a credential that can act as any user.
gaps.agent_memory_today: The docs describe short-lived tokens that SurrealDB Cloud brokers for members, keys that an admin mints in Studio, and self-service POST /keys. A self-service key belongs only to the principal of the caller. The docs mention no Entra or other single sign-on, and no longer show the route that brokers a token. A personal access token cannot make Cloud writes, so a new principal needs an interactive login.

gaps.name: Leak test tenant
gaps.need: SurrealDB provides a test tenant with a leak that SurrealDB introduces on purpose, so Spreetail can show that its leak test catches a leak. SurrealDB also gives advance notice of model and prompt changes.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory has no mode that switches permissions off, because every key belongs to a principal. The docs mention no test tenant, and no advance notice of model or prompt changes.

gaps.name: Origin keys
gaps.need: Each conversation, document, and measurement carries a required origin key from its system of record. A replay at any later time lands on the stored record.
gaps.agent_memory_today: An idempotency key holds for 24 hours only, and documents match only by a hash of their bytes. PUT /documents/{id} replaces a document and runs its pipeline again.

gaps.name: Defined wire behaviour
gaps.need: Each rule break returns its own error code. A request with an unknown field fails. Every write route accepts an idempotency key, so a retry is safe.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Each error body carries only a message; the HTTP status is the sole code. So two rule breaks with the same status differ only in free text. The server ignores a field that it does not know. Two pages offer an idempotency key on writes in general, but only the two fact routes are named.

gaps.name: Open recall pipeline
gaps.need: A recall widens each hit to every claim on its subject, and reranks the results by default. It packs them under a token budget that the caller sets.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Recall searches a pool of 256 candidates by default, and returns 50 hits at most. A cross-encoder pass that ranks the results again is a flag on document queries only. It needs a reranker from the deployment. Other recalls rank again, over a doubled pool, only when the first results are thin or weak. No request field limits a read by tokens.

gaps.name: Cost bounds
gaps.need: The cost of each operation stays bounded as the corpus grows. A revision touches only the claims that it changes.
gaps.agent_memory_today: The decay sweep runs once a day over all facts in the Context, though identity facts do not decay. Reads search a bounded pool of 256 candidates by default. The docs state no other cost bound for each operation.

gaps.name: Custom entity types
gaps.need: Spreetail can add its own entity types, such as the process nodes of the Spreetail process map, and tag each signal with them. Spreetail can also store an advisory record type, such as a bias, that Agent Memory never treats as a rule.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory has 12 fixed entity types, and two of them are only for system entities. It saves any other type as “other”.
gaps.ask_surrealdb: Ask for labels on every stored fact, or for a custom record type. This does not add entity types.

gaps.name: Own embedding model
gaps.need: Spreetail can select the embedding model, which turns text into vectors for search.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory accepts only the gemini-embedding-2 model, and the docs list Google as required for embeddings. The docs offer no other embedding model, and no reindex endpoint to embed stored data again.

gaps.name: Smaller asks
gaps.need: Extraction reuses the property names in use in a scope, so that one kind of fact has one name. Spreetail also asks for published isolation tests.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Extraction sees up to 500 entity names, with the most recently updated first, so an older name drops out. SurrealDB has SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, and a cure53 audit, but no published isolation tests for Agent Memory.

gaps.name: Reconciliation model setting
gaps.need: The marketing page calls the reconciliation hook “configurable per Context and per call”. The docs say that Agent Memory stores the reconciliation model setting but does not apply it. Which is true? Can the setting carry the contradiction policy of Spreetail?
gaps.agent_memory_today: If the docs are correct, reconciliation makes no model call, so the stored reconciliation model setting has no effect. One reconciliation setting does act: a confidence floor for each Context. It decides whether a scored value from the same source kind replaces the old one. No setting changes the rule that values from different source kinds both stay live. Then M3 needs a new feature, not a setting.

gaps.name: Confidence and writer of a fact
gaps.need: Does every fact that Agent Memory extracts from chat carry a confidence score? Does Agent Memory store on each attribute the principal that wrote it, or only in the decision traces and audit records?
gaps.agent_memory_today: The docs give part of the answer. Turns and documents share one extraction contract with a confidence field. But the confidence floor applies \"only when the new value carries an explicit confidence score\", so some values carry no score. The docs say that each decision trace records “the acting principal”. They also say principal ids \"appear throughout stored facts\", but no documented attribute field holds the writer. The answers decide how F1 compares authors and how M2 weights sources.

gaps.name: Docs consistency
gaps.need: Where the docs still contradict each other, which statement is correct? SurrealDB must give a written answer for each contradiction before the general release.
gaps.agent_memory_today: SurrealDB fixed four contradictions in the docs. Others remain, for example about relations that ended, asynchronous extraction, and the expiry setting. The count of eight in the 11 October version has no list behind it. The docs also disagree on whether a reversed instruction replaces the old instruction or stays active beside it.

gaps.name: Comparison across scopes
gaps.need: The background consolidation pass pools every scope. Does it compare, merge, or replace facts from scopes with different readers? Does it write its output where other principals can read it?
gaps.agent_memory_today: The reconciler compares values only within one scope. But the REST reference says that the background scheduler pass pools every scope. If that pass mixes scopes, the facts of one holder can change or reach another holder.

gaps.name: Entra connection
gaps.need: Spreetail connects its Entra tenant and its connectors to Agent Memory. Each Spreetail connector that sends content has its own identity, so that each connector can have its own trust.
gaps.agent_memory_today: The docs still say that SurrealDB Cloud brokers short-lived tokens for members, and that admins mint keys. They no longer show the route that brokers a token. Without F19, a proxy must act for users with the On-Behalf-Of header. That header gives the intersection of the grants of the proxy and of the user, so the proxy needs grants on every user scope.

gaps.name: Leak and quality tests
gaps.need: A test suite proves that one user cannot read the data of another user. The suite also catches the known leak in the F20 tenant. Quality tests run the labelled Spreetail corpus against Agent Memory.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory has no mode that switches permissions off. Without F20, the run that must fail can only use a principal with access to the whole Context.

gaps.name: Signals by node
gaps.need: Signals go to the owner of each business process, and Spreetail counts the signals for each process. Spreetail also keeps work state and provisional process nodes, and filters reads by tag and recency, with the documented API.
gaps.agent_memory_today: A search returns 50 hits at most and has no further pages. The paged lists return up to 500 records for each page, and the count=true option adds the total of the filtered set. The relation list filters by source or target entity, so one call may count the links to one node. No documented list filters by label, so a count by label needs many searches or a walk through the lists. This work relies on F25.

gaps.name: Capture from everyday tools
gaps.need: Spreetail captures knowledge from the tools that people already use, through the Agent Memory adapters. A draft for another person waits on the client until that person approves it.
gaps.agent_memory_today: The architecture page lists five adapters that send conversations to Agent Memory. They are LangChain, the Claude Code hook, OpenAI Agents, the Vercel AI SDK, and n8n. The integration pages confirm three of them. In n8n, a generic HTTP Request node calls the REST API. The LangChain page documents only query and reflect tools. The preview mode “extracts but does not persist”, so the client must send the write again to store it.

gaps.name: Export bundle
gaps.need: Spreetail can export a filtered set of claims at one point in time, as a manifest and one file for each claim.
gaps.agent_memory_today: Agent Memory has no export. The view of a Context as files through MCP is only planned.
